messages:
maria: FYI NimblePay hitting tps SLOs on their Dedicated pool, started ~14:32 UTC. Customers seeing 429 / admission_rejected and p50 latency spikes.

josh: copying logs now — looks like burst_credits are at 0 and headroom dropped to negative. suspect KV cache thrash after recent model rollout.

maria: they did roll to v2-quant last night. no other config changes. they report a lot more short chats (narrow prompts) -> probably lots of KV cache churn.

samir: can we confirm kvcache miss rate? I pulled ingress logs:
```
2026-03-15T14:32:11Z admit: reject token_rate=1520 limit=1200 headroom=-320 burst_credits=0 kvcache_miss_pct=92
2026-03-15T14:32:12Z serve: enqueue_time_ms=18 kvcache_hit=false seq_len=64
2026-03-15T14:32:12Z serve: gpu_util=78% batch=1
```

devon: 92% miss is huge. that will blow through headroom fast because we can't reuse KV. Also batch sizes are tiny (batch=1) so per-token cost is high.

kelsey: @autoscale-bot what happened with autoscaler around 14:30? I thought we had burst headroom configured for NimblePay.

autoscale-bot: Autoscaler event: scale_up 2 gpus at 14:31:24 UTC (policy=reserved_burst). New capacity available at 14:34:01 UTC.

maria: so there was a 3.5m gap between initial surge and capacity ready. meanwhile burst_credits exhausted. we need immediate mitigation for the customer and a playbook to avoid repeats.

josh: quick mitigation options (ranked):
1) Temporarily increase admission token limit for their pool (risky for noisy neighbor)
2) Force fallback to v1 model (better kv cache locality)
3) Increase per-customer reserved burst (billing implications)
4) Apply short-term request shedding for heavy short prompts (nth-percentile)

samir: repro steps for infra team to reproduce locally:
- use loadgen with many short prompts (avg seq=40, stddev 10)
- set concurrency to 200 requests/s targeting dedicated pool
- verify kvcache_miss_pct > 80% and burst_credits drop to 0 within ~90s

code snippet (loadgen):
```sh
for i in $(seq 1 300); do \
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    -d '{"model":"nimble-v2-quant","prompt":"Q$i","max_tokens":48}' &
done
wait
```

devon: ops suggestion: enable short-term kvcache warming by routing a fraction (~10%) of requests to pinned warmers for 60s after rollout. may reduce miss rate dramatically.

kelsey: customer is asking for rollback to v1. can support approve rollback if we think it's safe?

maria: approved for rollback to v1 for the next 2 hours while we monitor. coordinate with eng-runtime for a smooth rollout.

infra-bot: rollback job started for nimble-v2-quant -> nimble-v1 at 14:38:05 UTC.

samir: note for postmortem: autoscaler slow-start problem + kvcache-unfriendly model -> admission control starve. Need: faster warm capacity path, pre-warm job on model rollouts, and per-customer burst accounting changes.

josh: logging action items:
- samir: add kvcache_miss_pct to per-route alerts (P1)
- devon: prototype kvcache pinning/warmers (P2)
- kelsey: coordinate billing/backstop changes for reserved burst (P2)
- maria: notify NimblePay (done) and confirm rollback success

maria: NimblePay says rollback restored p50 below SLO after ~2m. they reported a handful of 429s during the window but no data loss. :thumbsup:

devon: follow-up: schedule a dedicated runbook to do a canary warm for model rollouts to avoid cold-kv spikes.

kelsey: I'll open a support ticket with recommended changes and add the customer's permission to test warmers on their traffic.

maria: thanks everyone. closing for now — we'll capture postmortem items in #postmortems once eng-runtime has an action plan.

infra-bot: Incident closed at 14:52:10 UTC. Severity: P2.
